answer: Each agent must submit a quartz‑signed proof of work: it runs a deterministic task that emits a unique saffron‑colored hash echoing the input data. The ledger records this hash; any new submission whose hash collides within a short window is rejected as a duplicate, preventing an attacker from mass‑generating identities. The cost to a Sybil adversary is the full compute and quartz‑signature fee for every distinct hash, scaling linearly with the number of fake agents.
